posts.name: grysqrl
posts.cooked:
Welcome to the forums! I'm glad you're enjoying the game. Haka can fill different roles depending on what the team needs him to be.

Primarily, he tends to be a damage dealer - Taiaha lets him deal consistent damage round after round. If the villain or environment have lots of targets, Haka can gobble them up with Savage Mana and spit them out later for a huge amount of damage. His damage output can be augmented by using Haka of Battle to increase the next damage he deals, which is nice for bringing down the villain (particularly villains with damage reduction, where lots of small attacks aren't very effective).

Haka can also tank pretty well. He's got a ton of hit points. Ta Moko reduces incoming damage, Haka of Shielding helps to block larger hits that you know are coming, and Haka of Restoration helps to keep you healthy. Enduring Intercession and Ground Pound help to protect your teammates.

You'll notice that some of his abilities require you to discard cards in order to use them (Haka cards and Ground Pound), so you have things like Dominion, Vitality Surge, and Mere to get more cards into your hand. Playing the Haka cards helps with this too; often, it's useful to play one just for the extra card draw and then discard one card that you don't need for a small bonus.

This is a simplified view of Haka, but I hope it helps a little. There are numerous strategy guides for the heroes here that might be useful for you.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Let me spin you a little anecdote.

Earlier tonight, I was playing Haka versus the Chairman. Due to some kind of crappy draws, early on about all I was able to do was play two copies of Dominion. Every time an environment card got killed off, Haka drew two. During the final turn of the game, Fanatic was dead and Absolute Zero and Nightmist were at 5 HP or lower; the Chairman still had 26 HP.

However, because Haka had been drawing cards like mad, I had 24 cards in hand. One of them was Haka of Battle. Since Haka had his Taiaha out…yeah, that was it. All she wrote. 26 HP of damage in a single strike.

The point of this anecdote is, between cards like the various Haka of [activity], Healing Surge, Mere, and Dominion, Haka should always have lots and lots of cards in his hand to allow him to adapt to what the party needs. If big damage is coming at him, he should be able to mitigate it with Haka of Shielding. If he’s low on HP, he should be able to heal himself. If a bad guy absolutely positively had to go down right now, Haka should have an option available to him. If anyone ever needs to discard to prevent some awful effect, Haka should have plenty of cards in hand.

Haka is what I would call a passive board controller. He can’t control an enemy’s deck like Visionary or Parse, but he can handle whatever the villain telegraphs coming his way.

posts.name: Killswitch
posts.cooked:
I like Haka because he's all about patience, but he's still quite useful in the meantime. You want him to build up his Savage Mana (which counters half the villians in the game), and also his hand size. Dominion helps with this a lot. Use it early and maximize your stockpile of resources later.

So what are you doing when you're not smashing things with charged up Taiyahas or Savage Mana piles? Well, some amazing cards include Rampage and Ground Pound. You can either do massive AoE, or negate damage from non-hero targets. Secondary support cards include Ta Moko and one of his weapons, Mere or Taiyaha. Haka doesn't have much trouble drawing into these resources, which makes him incredibly consistent. Eternal Haka is even better at tearing through his deck early. Prime Warden Haka will be good at lending his powers to his comrades, so someone else can heal up. Like Scholar!

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
I don't go for the huge hand insta-finish with Haka.

Haka of Battle is phenomenal for removing hard targets, ones with reduction or 5-6 HP that you want gone immediately.  I also don't play for Savage mana, although it is nice when you get it.  Even then I usually use it as soon as there is tangible benefit (like a Voss ship, Siege Breaker or nasty Apostate Relics.

 

Haka is a warrior, just pick the current biggest threat to your allies and knock it down.

As for Prime Warden Haka, my favorite moment so far with that power was Haka of Restoration when Scholar had three Energy forms in play to finish off the last three members of the Ennead in one shot.
